properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-06-21 to Rockdale Marcellus Llc in Liberty Twp, Tioga county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Rockdale Marcellus Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-06-21
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 853325
Permit API: 117-21998
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2019-06-21
Comments: Results from sample IDs 0718-020 through 022, collected on 5/13/19 as documented in inspection report 2879933, were received from the lab on 6/21/19. At the time of inspection, WQS Sara Metz observed water discharging from the pad into the infiltration basin. Conductivity of the discharge ranged from 0.999 to 1.669 mS/cm, and conductivity in the basin where the discharge was entering was 1.493 mS/cm. Elevated levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides in sample 0718-020, collected from the infiltration basin, indicate that the discharge was a pollutional substance. The discharge of a pollutional substance to the infiltration basin, considered Waters of the Commonwealth, is a violation of Section 401 of the Clean Streams Law. Elevated levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides in sample 0718-021, collected from a high-conductivity puddle (18.75 mS/cm) on the pad near a crushed containment berm, also indicate a release of a pollutional substance to the pad surface (as compared to sample 0718-022 collected from an area of the pad containing water with conductivity under 1 mS/cm). It is unclear whether this affected area is separate from or related to the affected area described in a previous Notice of Violation issued on 6/10/19 with inspection report 2890742. Results from sample IDs 0718-024 through 028, collected on 5/17/19 as documented in inspection report 2885414, were also received from the lab on 6/21/19. Elevated levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides were present in samples collected from the infiltration basin (0718-024) and the basin outfall pipe (0718-025). Additional samples collected from a PVC drain pipe discharge (0718-026) and the resulting flow path to Salt Spring Run (0718-027) show elevated levels of strontium and chlorides, as compared to background conditions in Salt Spring Run upstream of the pad location (0718-028). New violation noted. In addition, the following violations cited on 6/10/19 remain outstanding: 78a.66(b), 78a.56(a), Section 402(b) of the Clean Streams Law, and Section 301 of the Solid Waste Management Act.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/09/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 981256
Permit API: 117-21531
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Sullivan Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/09/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Seneca Resource's Hepler D 235 well site located in Sullivan Township, Tioga County on 1/9/2023 at 1030 hours. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of diesel fuel reported by Seneca Resources. Complaint tracking system (CTS) identification # 369178 is tied to this release within CTS. A diesel powered glycol heater had a pinhole leak in a fuel line that caused diesel fuel to release to an interior secondary containment which also had a leak, releasing diesel fuel to a secondary containment structure beneath the entire unit. The secondary containment structure on the ground was discovered to be leaking, which released a mixture of diesel fuel and stormwater to the ground surface. While onsite, company personnel evaluated the impacted area and determined the release to be estimated at 35 gallons of diesel fuel mixed with stormwater from the containment. Crew began by recovering all of the diesel on the surface with a portable vacuum unit. The glycol heater was then transferred to a new, functional secondary containment outside of the impacted area. Once a residual waste container arrived onsite, excavation of the impacted area began. A Seneca representative stated later that 1.5 to 2 inches of pad material was scraped from the impacted area. All impacted material was placed into a lined residual waste container for later disposal. Excavation and remedial activities were completed by 1300 hours on 1/9/2023. The glycol heater unit was repaired and it's secondary containment was replaced. No portion of the diesel fuel release was able to escape the pad surface.Based on the findings of this inspection report, the reported release made by Seneca Resources, and the timely remediation completed by the operator, violations of the following are cited against API #117-21531 as immediately corrected:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S. 691.402(b)I departed the site at 1130 hours.

Report Details

Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 949751
Permit API: 053-30563
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Harmony Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/29/2022
Comments: This is a follow up inspection pertaining to E&S violations along the lease roads used to access this well that were issued on 8/31/2021 (inspection # 3244669). There has been no apparent attempt at addressing the violations, as the roads are in the same condition that was documented on 8/31/2021. The access road leading to this well has not been properly maintained, which has led to any installed BMPs along this road to no longer function as designed. The road material has also broken down and is not properly shaped (crowned). These deficiencies have resulted in accelerated erosion of the road surface. Sections of this road are severely two tracked/rutted as there is no functional ditch and stormwater is forced to run down the running surface of the road. Road fabric that was put down along this road is exposed along numerous stretches of the road, this indicates that a significant amount of road material has eroded from this road due to a lack of maintenance. This location is located near several springs and an UNT of Pithole Run. This well (and several others on the Shattuck lease) were transferred to Stonehaven Energy soon after the aforementioned violations were issued. Jeremy Graham and I discussed necessary corrective actions last fall, which have not yet taken place. The well itself is currently not plumbed to any gathering lines and the engine has been removed from the pump jack. The well # and API # are displayed on the jack, a faded site ID sign stating Devonian Resources as the operator is also present on the location, this information should be updated to display Stonehaven as the current operator. These issues will be evaluated in future inspections and referred to the county OGI if necessary.

Comments: On February 8, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection at the Kiskiminetas Spring School 4 well in Loyalhanna Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3488724, where high conductivity was found underneath the brine tank valve. The Department had yet to receive the waste manifest from remediation or the quantity released in the spill noted in IR 3307023, therefore the Department was unable to assess whether the spill had been remediated in accordance with DEP Spill Policy. Violations were continued as a result, and the Department requested that the operator provide the waste manifest and any other relevant information no later than February 10, 2023. Heavy tire rutting was also observed on the access road. Present were myself, DEP OGI Curtis Small, Brian Haney from PA Mineral Services, and Joe Miller from Mid Atlantic Energy Services. The following was observed:The well site appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no concerns related to E and S or vegetative coverage (see photo 7). The API number and operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 4). This information now reflects the information that the Department has on file. A hissing sound and a strong gas odor was observed coming from the well head at the time of inspection (see photo 5). Mr. Haney and Mr. Miller were making repairs on the well head at the time of inspection. The brine tank appeared to be sound at the time of inspection (see photo 3). However, elevated conductivity remains underneath the brine tank valve (see photo 1). A background soil conductivity reading was taken along the access road, which read 120 Microsiemens (see photo 9). Heavy tire rutting remains in the access road (see photo 8). It was initially noted that the access road is shared with the operator and Kiski Prep School. However, Mr. Haney informed the Department that unrelated timber trucks also use the access road for removal of trees for timber. Trees that are said to be marked for timber use could be observed north of the well site (see photo 6).Based on observations from this inspection, the the Department recommends that the operator investigate the cause of the elevated conductivity and remediate accordingly. Violations remain outstanding. The Department also recommends that the operator cooperatively monitor and maintain the access road with Kiski School, and Timber companies that use it to prevent accelerated erosion. The Department requests that the operator provide the waste manifest and any other relevant information, including quantity released no later than February 10, 2023.

Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/22/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8198934
Permit API: 117-22210
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/22/2024
Comments: On 8/22/2024 at 1100 hrs., Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) representative John Rogers conducted an Incident - Response to Accident or Event Inspection (INCDT) of the Seneca Resources - Bauer 849 well pad located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. Complaint Id: 383218. It was 66 and partly cloudy when I arrived at the site.When I arrived at the site, I met Seneca's company man, Adam Pierce. Adam explained current operations as follows: A Nextier frac fleet is on site performing stimulation operations on seven recently drilled wells. The crew is currently zippering between 64HU, 66HU and 67HU wells with the other four wells already completed. Adam expects the crew to be done fracking the wells by August 24, 2024.Adam showed me where the spill event occurred. Tighe Truman joined us during the inspection. A water hauling truck like the one shown in pictures 3, 4 and 5 was backed up to the frac tanks located along the south edge of the pad. The truck driver was running the on-board air pump to provide air pressure to help push the liquids out of the tank. While the water truck was pressuring up, a pop-off valve valve that was connected to the top hatch on the front of the tank released pressure and released an estimated 20 gallons of produced water from the tank, the liquids impacting the ground under the truck and flowing a short distance east. The truck driver was at the controls on the side of the truck and immediately stopped pressuring the truck. Normally the pop-off valve should be above the fluid level but the front wheels of the truck were parked in a small depression that allowed the level of fluid to be above the pop-off connection. Discussing this incident with Adam and Tighe, the normal operating pressure is unknown and the pressure that the pop-off released at is unknown. It was unknown at the time of this inspection if the valve failed and opened below the designed relief pressure or if the driver allowed the pressure in the tank to exceed the designed pop-off relief pressure. Adam did say that it was a new driver and believes that the driver did not open the discharge valve on the truck before applying pressure. Adam commented that with the small air pocket of a fully loaded truck, it would only take a short amount of time to build up pressure. The area of the release is shown in pictures 3 and 6. The surface of the area has been scraped and new gravel has been installed. The scraped material was placed into a rolloff dumpster that, due to a previous spill, was already stationed at the site. The dumpster is lined and staged in secondary containment. Water in the truck offloading catch basin field tested at 11.06 mS conductance. Water in the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 19.49 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance liquids with Adam who said that he would have employees continue cleaning out the containments.The release of well-bore fluids to the unprotected pad surface constitutes violations of these three regulations; SWMA 301, CSL 402(b) and 25 PA Code 78a.56. The spill had been cleaned up, resulting in VIOICs (Violation noted and Immediately Corrected).The DEP recommends the following: 1. Discuss with the trucking company the need to inspect the equipment involved with this incident to ensure it is in serviceable condition. The pop-off valve should be examined to determine if it operated correctly or failed. Remove/repair equipment as necessary.2. Ensure personnel are trained on the safe and proper procedure for offloading fluids from tanker trucks.3. Screen the area impacted by the release of well-bore fluids for additional contamination and continue with cleanup as necessary.4. Continue to remove the elevated conductance fluid from the frac tank secondary containment and the unloading catch basin. Train personnel on proper procedures to prevent releasing the elevated conductance fluids into the containments. I left the site at 1230 hours.

Comments: Follow-up inspection conducted to assess conditions on and off the pad. Both the 2H and 4H wells continue to flow back. A puddle in front of the west containment next to the MASS had a conductivity of 16.6 mS/cm. Another puddle to the south, not directly in front of the containment, had a conductivity of 4.96 mS/cm. Soil conductivity readings in this area ranged from 1.3 to >4 mS/cm when measured with the soil conductivity meter. On the main pad surface, the conductivity of puddles on the surface near the gravel piles remains elevated with conductivities above 2 mS/cm here. The area between the well heads, which had elevated conductivities during the previous inspection, has been back-filled with new gravel. After speaking with Taylor Parsons of Falcon on site about my conductivity readings, he accompanied me to the MASS. I showed him that the Oakton conductivity meter was showing that the puddles in front and to the south of the west containment were elevated. I took a conductivity reading of the fluid inside the containment which was >19.99 mS/cm. He stated that the containment may not be adequate for preventing spills of produced water to the surface when water trucks are off-loading the MASS. He said that he would have a more substantial area of containment built which would allow the trucks to drive onto the containment, which he believed would prevent produced water from getting onto the surface of the MASS pad. A contractor, Blood Hound, was on site when I arrived. The contractor marked the location of the PVC Pipe with spray paint and flags. The path is included as a red line in the map in photo #3. The attached maps and tables show the conductivity readings recorded during this inspection. Outstanding violations.

Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Springville Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/27/2025
Comments: On 10/27/25 I was at the Coterra Energy Lauer D. Well Site from 1327 to 1459 hours to perform a follow up inspection in response to the report a release of an unknown volume of natural gas and production fluid out of the Lauer D 12H well on 10/22/25. The weather conditions are mostly sunny skies with a light wind and temperatures in the low to mid 50's. The intent of the inspection is to evaluate the impact to the ground surface of the well pad from the release of production fluid. Shortly after arrival I met with Brendon Logan, Environmental Health and Safety Specialist. We walked to the location on the site where a sump (Sump # 1) was constructed on 10/22/25 in a drainage channel adjacent to and west of the access road near the well pad entrance. Sump # 1 is collecting fluid which released out of the 12H well onto the well pad and flowed into a drainage channel on the western side of the pad. Fluid in Sump # 1 is transferred via a pump into a frac tank in a containment structure. I utilized a Hanna HI 98331 Groline Soil Test Meter and an Oakton PCTS 5 meter to perform field screening of specific conductance (electrical conductivity, EC) in wet soil in the drainage channel adjacent to Sump #1 and in fluid pooled in this sump. Mr. Logan and I walked in a counter clockwise direction starting in the infiltration basin south of the well pad and in between the tank pad and well pad around the perimeter of the pad in the basin, to the northeast corner of the pad, then across the north side of the pad, and then to the center of the pad near the wells. I also performed conductivity screening in wet soil and fluid in the infiltration basin south and east of the well pad inside of the LOD and on the pad surface near the wells and equipment designated for frac operations. Conductivity readings in fluid in Sump # 1 and in a sump constructed just east and adjacent to the access road and south of the well pad in an infiltration basin, (Sump#2), and on the well pad, are indicative of a spill of production fluid. I also met with Brody Webster, Andy Mehalko, and Mike Oakley of Coterra during the inspection. Coterra is in the process of preparing to remediate (clean up) impacted pad material in association with the release of production fluid. Coterra has removed a section of the secondary containment liner near the wells and rig mats in order to evaluate the extent of the impact and remove impacted material. Coterra informed me that they plan to remove additional equipment designated for frac operations and commence the remediation process via the use of heavy equipment tomorrow, 10/29/25. See photos for additional details. Please feel free to contact me @ 570-346-5533 or jsassi@pa.gov should you have any questions.

Comments: On June 22 2023, the Department conducted an inspection of the Prigg Morgan 11272 Well Site due to an incident. Accompaying in today's inspection was Derek Zofchak (Range Resource Representative), Nick Reda (Range Resource Representative) and Tyler Metzger (ET DEP)The findings were as follows:This inspection is in response to several E and S BMP failures on the Prigg Morgan Well Site. In a phone call from Range Resource Representative Dennis Furmacek, they reported that they had 3 separate sections of temporary E and S BMP silt sox were overtopped and or displaced. This resulted in sediment to leave the LOD and settle into adjacent vegetative field. The failures were identified during a post precipitation inspection conducted on 6/16/2023. Mr. Furmacek also indicated that waters of the commonwealth were not threatened and sediment was not discharged into the waters of the commonwealth. During today's inspection, the Act 9 Sign was on site but not permanently installed. The access road appeared to be stable with no observed erosion or sedimentation concerns. The ESCGP drawings, PPC plan and ER plan were on site. Also on site was the site inspection records for 6/16/2023 recording the E and S BMP silt sox overtopping and 6/19/2023 which recorded the remediation efforts at the well site. The CFS that was effected in the three different locations were all re-staked. Each area that was affected outside of the LOD were mulched and reseeded.Based on today's inspection, The Department will conduct a subsequent inspection to continue to evaluate remediation efforts.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/29/2023
Comments: On March 29 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to an OGI request of the James Joshowtiz 12 OG Well.The findings were as follows:At the time of the inspection, The access road appeared to be stable with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. The well site exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. There were no erosion or sedimentation issues onsite. The well posting was present at the time of this inspection. There were no observed leaks or discharge on the ground or around the wellhead. The production tank appears to have a corrosive pipe connected to it that is actively leaking fluid. A soil conductivity reading was taken at the base of the production tank. The soil conductivity reading was 15.78mS were the active leaking fluid is occurring. A background soil conductivity reading was taken of 0.22 mS. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the area as necessary in accordance with the Department's Spill Policy. The Department requests the operator provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred. The Department request that this information be provided in the NOV response. Based on today's observations, violations are being issued at this time.
